kinds.subroutine: runtime routine called with CALL, as its Fortran form says
kinds.function: runtime routine that returns a value, as its Fortran form says

tags.offload: runs on or moves data to a device (offloading)
tags.par: starts parallel execution on the device
tags.loop: applies to the loop that follows

fields.pg: page of the specification PDF that prints the heading of the section that documents it

legend.keys: directive names lower case with blanks between words (enter data; host_data keeps its underscore); clauses and routines lower case; environment variables upper case

libgomp.rule: routines and environment variables; _ is written _005f (acc_get_num_devices → acc_005fget_005fnum_005fdevices)

parallel.s: Offloads a block to the device, run by gangs of workers with vector lanes.

serial.s: Offloads a block to the device, run by one gang of one worker.

kernels.s: Offloads a block whose loops the compiler turns into device kernels.

parallel loop.s: A parallel construct whose only content is a loop construct.

serial loop.s: A serial construct whose only content is a loop construct.

kernels loop.s: A kernels construct whose only content is a loop construct.

data.s: Maps data to the device for the duration of the enclosed block.

enter data.s: Maps data to the device until a matching EXIT DATA.

exit data.s: Ends the device mapping of data, copying it back if asked.

host_data.s: In the block, the listed host variables refer to their device addresses.

loop.s: Describes how the following loop is spread over gangs, workers and vector lanes.

cache.s: Asks for array elements to be kept in the fastest device memory.

declare.s: Maps variables to the device for the lifetime of their scope.

init.s: Initialises the runtime for a device type.

shutdown.s: Shuts down the connection to a device.

set.s: Sets the default device or async queue.

update.s: Copies data between the host and the device.

wait.s: Waits for asynchronous operations to complete.

routine.s: Compiles a procedure for the device, with its level of parallelism.

async.s: Runs the construct asynchronously, on the given queue.

attach.s: Attaches device pointers to their targets’ device copies.

auto.s: Lets the compiler decide how to parallelise the loop.

bind.s: The name of the device version of a routine.

collapse.s: Applies the loop directive to the given number of nested loops.

copy.s: Copies the data to the device at entry and back at exit.

copyin.s: Copies the data to the device at entry.

copyout.s: Copies the data back from the device at exit.

create.s: Allocates the data on the device, without copying.

default.s: default(none) or default(present): the data attributes of variables not listed.

device_resident.s: Allocates the variables on the device only.

device_type.s: The following clauses apply only to the given device types.

deviceptr.s: The listed pointers already hold device addresses.

finalize.s: Sets the reference counts to zero, so the data is freed (EXIT DATA).

firstprivate.s: Private copies, initialised from the original variables.

if.s: Runs the construct on the device only if the condition is true.

if_present.s: Skips variables that are not on the device.

independent.s: The loop iterations are independent, so they may run in parallel.

link.s: Makes a global variable available on the device, allocated when it is used.

no_create.s: Uses the device copy if there is one, else the host data.

nohost.s: The routine is compiled for the device only.

num_workers.s: The number of workers per gang.

present.s: The data must already be on the device.

private.s: Each gang, worker or vector lane gets its own copy of the listed variables.

reduction.s: Combines the private copies with an operator (+, max, …) at the end.

self.s: Runs the construct on the local device (the host), or copies to the host (UPDATE).

use_device.s: In the block, the listed variables refer to their device addresses.

vector.s: Spreads the loop over vector lanes.

wait.s: Waits for the given async queues before starting.

worker.s: Spreads the loop over the workers of a gang.

acc_get_num_devices.s: Returns the number of devices of a device type.

acc_set_device_type.s: Sets the device type used for compute regions.

acc_get_device_type.s: Returns the device type used for compute regions.

acc_set_device_num.s: Sets the device used for compute regions.

acc_get_device_num.s: Returns the device used for compute regions.

acc_get_property.s: Returns a numeric property of a device, such as its memory size.

acc_get_property_string.s: Returns a text property of a device, such as its name or vendor.

acc_init.s: Initialises the runtime for a device type.

acc_shutdown.s: Disconnects the program from a device type.

acc_async_test.s: Returns whether the operations on an async queue have completed.

acc_wait.s: Waits for the operations on an async queue to complete.

acc_wait_all.s: Waits for every async queue to complete.

acc_on_device.s: Returns whether the code runs on the given device type.

acc_free.s: Frees device memory allocated with acc_malloc (C).

acc_copyin.s: Copies data to the device (allocating it there if needed).

acc_create.s: Allocates data on the device, without copying.

acc_copyout.s: Copies data back from the device and frees the device copy.

acc_delete.s: Frees the device copy of data.

acc_update_device.s: Copies data from the host to its device copy.

acc_update_self.s: Copies data from its device copy to the host.

acc_is_present.s: Returns whether data is present on the device.
